It returns the resulting array of negated cells together with the total time charged.

nodes.title: Length of a tour in the symmetric TSP

nodes.summary: The symmetric traveling salesperson problem is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of symmetric TSP instances, to an instance $(n, w, B)$ that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that fail to decode, and bitstrings that decode to instances that are not well formed, are rejected.
nodes.title: Symmetric TSP as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A symmetric TSP instance $(n, w, B)$ is feasible when there is a list of $n$ pairwise distinct natural numbers containing every $v < n$, that is, an ordering of the cities $0, 1, \dots, n-1$ visiting each exactly once, whose tour length with respect to $w$ (the sum of the weights of consecutive edges, including the return edge) is at most $B$.
nodes.title: Feasible symmetric TSP instances

nodes.summary: An instance of the symmetric traveling salesperson problem is a triple $(n, w, B)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of cities, a weight matrix $w$ given as a finite list of rows, each a finite list of natural numbers, and a natural number $B$, the bound.
nodes.title: Symmetric TSP instances

nodes.summary: The symmetric traveling salesperson decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: TRAVELING SALESPERSON (SYMMETRIC) is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A symmetric TSP instance $(n, w, B)$ is well formed when $n > 0$, the weight matrix $w$ has exactly $n$ rows and each row has exactly $n$ entries, $w$ is symmetric, that is $w_{a,b} = w_{b,a}$ for all $a, b < n$, and $w$ has zero diagonal, that is $w_{a,a} = 0$ for all $a < n$. Rows and columns are numbered from $0$.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
